macro_headline: Oil Volatility Drives Fed Hawkish Turn

macro_cards.title: MARKETS SELLING OFF — SPY $660.5 DOWN 0.16%, VIX 25+
macro_cards.body: Major indices closed lower Thursday with SPY at $660.5, down from $661.54. QQQ fell to $594 (-0.14%) while DIA dropped to $461.06 (-0.44%). The VIX spiked above 25 as geopolitical tensions and oil volatility rattled risk assets. Pre-market futures show modest recovery with ES +17.75 and NQ +51.75, but momentum remains fragile. Small caps outperformed with IWM gaining 0.62% to $247.59, suggesting some rotation into domestic plays. Defense and energy sectors led gains while tech mega-caps faced selling pressure.

macro_cards.title: OIL SHOCK — BRENT BRIEFLY $119, WTI $93.14 DOWN 2.4%
macro_cards.body: Crude oil markets experienced extreme volatility with Brent crude spiking to $119 per barrel before retreating. WTI settled at $93.14, down $2.41 from highs. Iran's attacks on Gulf energy facilities including Qatar sites injected severe supply shock fears. USO ETF fell 3.57% to $117.36 as markets digested potential $166 barrel scenarios if Strait of Hormuz closure persists. Treasury Secretary Bessent floated easing sanctions on Iranian oil already loaded on tankers to shore up supplies. Energy companies and defense contractors remain primary beneficiaries of this crisis.

macro_cards.title: FED HAWKISH HOLD — NO RATE CUTS PRICED FOR 2026
macro_cards.body: The Federal Reserve held rates steady Wednesday as inflation concerns trump labor market weakness. Bond traders eliminated all expectations for rate cuts this year following the decision. PPI surged 0.7% MoM in February, well above the 0.3% forecast, marking the biggest monthly jump in over a year. Powell's hawkish tone emphasized inflation risks from energy price spikes. 10-year yields rose to 4.28%, pressuring rate-sensitive growth stocks. Mortgage rates jumped above 6.22%, further dampening housing market prospects. The Fed's dual mandate is clearly tilting toward inflation control over employment support.

macro_cards.title: CONSUMER WEAKNESS — SPENDING DOWN 9% YOY AMID INFLATION
macro_cards.body: Consumer Edge reports sporting goods spending declined 9% year-over-year in the three months ended January 2026, highlighting broad discretionary weakness. Tariffs, inflation, and middle-income pressure are weighing on non-essential purchases. This follows broader retail headwinds as consumers prioritize necessities over discretionary items. Home Depot fell 0.83% to $328.18, reflecting concerns about big-ticket purchases. Consumer staples and value plays may outperform as spending patterns shift. The data suggests recession risks are mounting despite equity market resilience.

macro_cards.title: DEFENSE SUPERCYCLE — $200B PENTAGON REQUEST, CONTRACTOR SURGE
macro_cards.body: The Defense Department requested over $200 billion for Iran war operations and stock replenishment. Defense billionaire fortunes surged $28 billion in 20 days of conflict, highlighting the sector's profit potential. Palantir gained 2.04% to $155.87 on continued military AI demand. Kratos held steady at $92.75 while Palo Alto Networks rose 0.48% to $169.71. The arms race dynamic is accelerating with global military spending at record levels. Defense contractors face multi-year order visibility as geopolitical tensions remain elevated. This represents a structural shift toward higher defense budgets globally.

macro_cards.title: MICRON PARADOX — RECORD REVENUE BUT STOCK FALLS 3.2%
macro_cards.body: Micron reported record AI-fueled revenue but shares dropped 3.22% to $446.89 on margin peak concerns and aggressive capex spending. The CEO stated the company can't deliver enough memory to key customers, highlighting supply constraints. Despite blowout fundamentals, investors are questioning whether margins have peaked and future growth rates. This reflects broader market skepticism toward AI beneficiaries trading at premium valuations. Memory demand remains robust but execution risks are rising. The disconnect between fundamentals and stock performance suggests caution in semiconductor momentum trades.

macro_cards.title: SPACE TECH MOMENTUM — NVIDIA GTC SHOWCASES ORBITAL DATA CENTERS
macro_cards.body: CEO Jensen Huang unveiled plans for AI data centers in space, marking a new frontier for compute infrastructure. Applied Digital gained 0.21% to $26.71 while CoreWeave fell 2.6% to $80.69 on broader tech selling. The space computing theme could accelerate as terrestrial data center constraints mount. NuScale Power held steady at $11.99 as nuclear power gains traction for AI workloads. SpaceX AI initiatives with Tesla's continued chip orders at scale demonstrate the converging mega-trends. This represents a long-term structural growth opportunity beyond current market volatility.

macro_cards.title: CRYPTO SELLOFF — BITCOIN DROPS BELOW $70K AMID RISK-OFF
macro_cards.body: Bitcoin fell below $70,000 for the first time in over a week as energy price surges triggered broad risk asset selling. The Fed's hawkish stance strengthened the dollar, pressuring crypto valuations. Over $450 million in crypto liquidations occurred in 24 hours as bullish positions unwound. Crypto.com announced 12% workforce cuts citing AI integration, adding to sector headwinds. The correlation between crypto and risk assets remains high during geopolitical stress. Institutional adoption continues but macro headwinds are overwhelming fundamental support. Recovery depends on stabilization of oil prices and Fed policy outlook.

macro_cards.title: KEY CATALYSTS — EARNINGS SEASON WINDS DOWN, FED SPEAK AHEAD
macro_cards.body: With Q4 earnings largely complete, focus shifts to forward guidance and Fed communications. Notable upcoming catalysts include March PMI data (March 22), consumer confidence (March 25), and Core PCE inflation (March 28). Fed speakers including Powell, Williams, and Bullard will likely reinforce the hawkish pivot given oil price developments. Nvidia's GTC conference wraps up with potential AI infrastructure announcements. Geopolitical developments in the Gulf remain the key wildcard for energy prices and market sentiment. Options expiration next Friday could amplify volatility in current environment.
